correctness.rationale: For common Y~Gamma(2,beta), CHME X=Y/(2Z) with Z~Beta(q,q) and SME X=Y/U with U~Beta(q,1). A small-Z beta density z^(q-1)/B(q,q) gives K_C=E[Y^q]/(q 2^q B(q,q))=(q+1)2^-q beta^q Gamma(2q)/Gamma(q); SME gives K_S=E[Y^q]=beta^q Gamma(q+2). Thus R=2^-q Gamma(2q)/(q Gamma(q)^2). For q<=1, q B(q,q)>=1, so R<1. For q>=1, dlog R/dq=log2-int_0^inf exp(-qt)/(1+exp(t/2))dt>log2-1/(2q)>0; R(2)=3/4 and R(3)=5/4 yield a unique crossing q*=2.578543315125812... . Positive density asymptotics integrate to survival, giving hazards q/x, moment cutoff r<q, and quantile ratio R^(1/q). At q=1 the two denominators are identically distributed uniforms, so X_C= X_S/2 in distribution. Independent high-precision gamma/beta arithmetic reproduced the root and q=1,2,3 ratios.

value.rationale: The CHME publication explicitly motivates its new symmetric-beta construction through heavier tails than SME. The strict crossover, not merely generic shared tail exponents, supplies an actionable mathematical comparison in heavy-tail model choice.
